Key observations from the test image:
- Corn stalk broken/snapped at a **node**
- The node area has **intense black/dark brown discoloration**
- White/cream pith tissue visible inside the break
- Clean snap at the node level
- No shredded pith, no white mold, no obvious sclerotia

This strongly suggests **Physoderma_stalk_rot** (black nodes, snapping at first/second node) or possibly **Bacterial_stalk_rot**. Let me view reference images for both top candidates plus a few others.

The Physoderma_stalk_rot reference images are an excellent match — especially the bottom-left image showing a stalk broken cleanly at a **black node**, which is identical to the test image. Bacterial stalk rot shows wilted/collapsed plants, not matching.

Let me confirm with a couple more reference images.
Neither Anthracnose (shiny black rind, shredded pith) nor Diplodia (lodged stalks, brown pith, pycnidia) matches the test image. Let me view a few more to fulfill the minimum requirement.

Charcoal stalk rot shows shredded gray pith with tiny sclerotia — not matching. Fusarium shows ear kernel rot — not matching.

## Summary of Evidence

**Test image features:**
- Stalk snapped cleanly at a **node**
- Node area is **intensely black/dark brown**
- White/cream pith exposed at the break
- The plant was manually bent/broken showing the clean node snap

**Comparison:**
| Class | Match? | Key distinction |
|---|---|---|
| **Physoderma_stalk_rot** | ✅ **Strong** | Black nodes, stalk snaps at 1st/2nd node — exact match |
| Bacterial_stalk_rot | ❌ | Soft slimy rot with foul odor, vascular strands intact, plant wilts |
| Anthracnose_stalk_rot | ❌ | Shiny black rind streaks, shredded pith |
| Diplodia_stalk_rot | ❌ | Shredded pith, small black pycnidia |
| Charcoal_stalk_rot | ❌ | Gray charred appearance, tiny sclerotia |

The test image is an exact match for Physoderma_stalk_rot: the characteristic **completely black node** with the stalk snapping cleanly at that point is the defining feature of this disease.
